bug_semantics: mailparser textToHtml() auto-linkifies URLs found in text/plain email bodies and interpolates them as ${link.text} without neutralizing quotes. A crafted URL such as http://example.com?"onmouseover="alert('XSS')" terminates the double-quoted href attribute and injects an event-handler attribute; consumers that render the resulting textAsHtml then execute attacker script in the victim browser (CWE-79). flaw_origin: The exploitable mechanism was first assembled in 7cba5bcfc2591088b02b238a495e4e741825205c (v2.7.0, 2019-05-01). That commit switched textToHtml from he.encode(str) then linkify.match(encoded) to linkify.match(str) on the raw body, encoding only the non-link slices, while still interpolating unsanitized link.url/link.text. The unescaped href template itself was first written earlier in 8d544ffd8452bfae81b6e1fb22e78f488a843cc0 (2018-07-24) by dropping he.encode of url/text, but that parent still HTML-encoded the whole string before matching, so a raw quote never reached the attribute delimiter. 7cba5bc is a single-parent direct commit (no PR members to decompose); it is the smallest public first-write of match-on-raw-text plus unescaped interpolation.
